title: The Concept of Social Capital in Modern Communities
text:
Social capital refers to the networks of relationships among people who live and work within a particular society. These networks generate resources that can be leveraged by individuals or groups, such as trust, reciprocity, and shared norms.

Academic research posits that strong community ties act as buffers against economic downturns and social instability. High levels of social capital facilitate collective action and governance, improving overall public welfare beyond what material wealth alone can achieve. Therefore, investments in local civic engagement and institutional participation are key methods for strengthening these foundational community assets.
